correctness.rationale: The main threshold and escape laws are proved, but the last sentence of the Finding literally calls the entire diagonal a bounded invariant set. It is an unbounded invariant set on which every individual orbit is bounded (all diagonal points enter the bounded diagonal segment with coordinate at most M in absolute value in one step). Independently, the mean is bounded after one step, the negative endpoint has strictly inward drift at large transverse magnitude, and the positive endpoint has strictly outward drift there. At the latter endpoint the mean contracts geometrically, and a finite transverse limit would give nonzero limiting drift. The transverse magnitude grows at most linearly, so |uv| tends to zero; this controls the Gaussian ratio at v±u. For s=v² this gives Δs∼2a s² exp(−s), hence Δ[exp(s)/(2a s²)]→1 and both stated asymptotics. In the expanding regime the bounded-forcing variation-of-constants sum converges absolutely, and the geometric lower bound after threshold crossing makes its normalized limit nonzero. The verification note and Python source were inspected, not executed; their finite tests are not needed for these deductions.
